On behalf of the SASA Executive, I am pleased to welcome you to the August 2026 issue of the SASA Newsletter. The year seems to be moving faster than ever, and it is hard to believe that spring is already knocking on our doors. SASA continues to achieve remarkable milestones in 2026, particularly through our growing partnerships, and we are proud to celebrate the continued growth and strong support of our membership.

As stated in the previous Newsletter Issue, the SASA2026 conference will be hosted by University of the Witwatersrand (Wits) in Johannesburg, at the Birchwood Hotel and OR Tambo Conference Centre, conveniently located near OR Tambo International Airport. The conference will take place during the week of 23–27 November 2026 and will include two days of engaging and thought-provoking workshops at the start of the programme that are facilitated by distinguished invited speakers from both national and international institutions. Please diarise the event and register for the conference now, if you have not already done so. Also, be sure to submit your abstract by no later than the 31st of August deadline. SASA2026 promises to be yet another engaging and memorable event, and I look forward to welcoming you all to Johannesburg.

I am pleased to announce that a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between SASA and Statistics South Africa (Stats SA) was signed on 11 June 2026 at the Stats SA Headquarters, ISIbalo House, in Pretoria. The MoU provides a structured basis for collaboration between the two organisations to advance the discipline and application of statistics in South Africa. The signing of the MoU marks a significant milestone for both SASA and Stats SA. As you may be aware, the negotiation process has taken almost two years, making this achievement particularly noteworthy. More details, including relevant links, are provided in the sections that follow in this newsletter. I strongly encourage SASA members to take advantage of the opportunities presented by this MoU and to actively engage in initiatives that will help translate the agreement into meaningful and impactful activities.

Guided by a clear vision, strong sense of purpose, and steadfast commitment to excellence, SASA continues to strengthen its partnerships and collaborative networks. The SASA EC remains actively engaged with the Institute for Mathematical Sciences and Applications (IMSA) and other sister associations, including South African Mathematical Society (SAMS), Southern Africa Mathematical Sciences Association (SAMSA), and Mathematical Sciences Strategic Alliance (MSSA), among others. These partnerships play an important role in advancing the mathematical and statistical sciences and strengthening collaboration within the broader scientific community.

The new SASA Constitution, which was presented at the SASA AGM last year, is nearing completion and will soon be ready for implementation. Our Special Interest Groups (SIGs) remain actively engaged in hosting seminars and attracting new members who share common academic and professional interests. The SASA EC encourages members to join existing SIGs or propose new ones to contribute to the advancement of the discipline.

As your President, I also encourage you to support the South African Statistical Journal (SASJ) by submitting manuscripts for consideration for publication, as well as papers for inclusion in conference proceedings following our annual conferences. Your contributions are essential to strengthening SASA's scholarly activities and promoting the visibility and impact of our discipline.

Wishing you all the very best for the remainder of 2026!

I look forward to welcoming you all to the SASA Conference in November.

Daniel
